story_review.one_viewing_summary: Planned chain, not observed pixels. Flood water tops a San Antonio curb, swings the fence post's orange tag and climbs to the ankle mark by 1.0 s while the porch phone stays dark, then the warning lands late. The prototype station stands at the curb in shallow water, its panel charges, and a dashed line toward a cell tower stops halfway. Water rises past its four lenses and each lights. The opened housing, still on its post, sends readings to the chip, which lights a large lamp and a risk bar, while a dark server across the road is never reached. Rings run down a long street to the hub, then across open country, with the station in an inset, to the hub's mast. A seated responder works at a flood map where paths spread along the creek. On a curb notice board the 98.82% card fills and a blank field result card is stamped none reported. A finger reads the blank paper map. A technician folds the deployment plan into the prototype's closed case and latches it.
story_review.opening_to_ending: The opening question asks whether a station can judge rising street water with no power line and no cell tower. The water-before-warning stake now has a picture. The mechanism chain (charge, four lenses, local chip judgment, radio to the hub, flood map) answers yes as a design. The limits stay in the curb world: validation only, no field result, and the announcement names no installation. The close keeps the plan with the uninstalled prototype toward the stated goal, without a lift, departure or installed station, so no unreported outcome is promised.
story_review.weakest_transition: s6 to s7 at 40.94 s. The cut goes from the hub's flood map, an interior wall view, to the outdoor curb notice board. Location changes and only the amber accent carries over; no object crosses the cut. The place is now physical rather than an olive card, but the cut needs the phone review to show a muted viewer still links the validation card to the station.
